executive_summary:
Eight opportunities went into the final gate. Three earned INVEST, two EXPLORE, one WATCH, two REJECT - and the finding that matters most is not the ranking but its shape: none of the three funded items is a new product. OPP-07 The Other Half (rank 1, 68.8) is a women's block-and-proportion input plus two free internal sell-through pulls. OPP-03 Twenty Washes (rank 2, 59.0) is a make standard and a buy discipline on garments already in the line. OPP-02 Found Outdoors (rank 3, 55.5) is a naming, laddering and rack-legibility action on FN2659, a SKU Nike already ships in the doors it needs. All three survive only in DE-SCOPED form; the red team turned each from a franchise into an input. The engine's own conclusion about this category is capture, not invention - the growth it can evidence is in making existing shorts findable, durable, correctly proportioned and correctly sized, not in a new short. That is also the most uncomfortable finding here, because a capture programme produces no image for a line review.

Three structural facts govern everything above. First, the cross-dataset audit found no first-party Nike commercial data anywhere in the base and not one price confirmed against a retrieved page, with three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders coexisting - so every price and every length in all eight briefs is unanchored. Five of eight briefs proposed a new price rung; all have been struck. Second, the systemic failure across all seven specialists, flagged identically by all seven skeptics, was proposing product Nike already ships: the DNA UV Woven (FN2659) alone closed four independently declared white spaces. Third, roughly three quarters of the evidence is US-derived, while the stated SS28 priority space (Worldball, centred on Greater China) rests on evidence sourced almost entirely from outside China.

What needs a human decision: (a) whether to fund a capture portfolio at all when only OPP-07 sits inside a named SS28 space and Uniform of Youth is served by nothing that survived; (b) OPP-06's Doha leg, the only item with an external clock - the FIBA product partnership expires in 2027 with no renewal found, and the LA28 leg is already killed on rights held by Fanatics, Ralph Lauren and FOURTEEN; (c) the EmpCo claims review, applicable 27 September 2026 and now a compliance item regardless of this portfolio; (d) an explicit adjacency plan, because four of eight briefs propose product against the same DNA/Icon rail. The decision gate is open. This document does not close it.
market_framing:
The global basketball shorts market, as evidenced here rather than as assumed: a flat-unit, price-and-mix business meeting a competitive field in retreat, with the shelf already discounting.

Nike's own audited disclosure (A03-S9) shows apparel growing about +2% currency-neutral on units +1%, with ASP growth coming from mix and already eroded by discounts, against roughly USD 1.5B of annualised tariff cost and 120bp of FY26 gross-margin headwind (A04-S8). The channel has inverted: wholesale +4% against ten consecutive quarters of Nike Digital decline (A02-S7, A04-S1, both VERIFIED), while every Western competitor retreats from performance basketball apparel (PAT-10). Greater China is Nike's weakest region in the same filings.

Demand is not uniformly soft. Women's basketball is the one signal the audit made STRONGER: three consecutive record seasons, a ratified CBA, verified Unrivaled event economics including roughly USD 400,000 of merchandise in one Philadelphia night (A05-S7), a retailer CEO's first-party call-out (A04-S5), and registry participation growth in a second country (A02-S9). Heat is the only functional need corroborated across physiology (A06-S2, 0.00-1.33 kg of trapped sweat), documented institutional behaviour change (A06-S5) and a competitor's multi-season commercial platform (A03-S7) - PAT-11.

Against that, the observable shelf refuses price: DNA 8 inch at 50% off, DNA 6 inch realised at USD 37.50, a USD 65 Sabrina clearing at USD 42.97, the Australian UV Woven at AUD 44.99, Kohl's Big and Tall Academy 11 inch at USD 27.75, Decathlon's Tarmak SH500 at GBP 5.99. Critically, no syndicated source isolates basketball shorts as a segment at all (A02-S1 after the audit stripped its CAGR). There is no market size for this category in this base that we would defend.
how_to_read_confidence:
Three different confidence numbers appear in this pipeline and they are not interchangeable. Read them in this order.

1. DEVELOPMENT confidence (0-100), set by the agent that wrote the brief, before challenge. Range here: 34 (OPP-05) to 62 (OPP-02). Treat as an author's self-assessment.

2. ADJUSTED confidence, set by the red-team challenger after attacking the brief. Every single one fell: OPP-01 52 to 26, OPP-02 62 to 40, OPP-03 60 to 48, OPP-04 61 to 38, OPP-05 34 to 24, OPP-06 57 to 39, OPP-07 61 to 41, OPP-08 58 to 44. Only OPP-01 was declared dead (survives=false). The uniform decline is the most honest number in the file: no brief got stronger under attack, and the average drop is roughly 17 points.

3. PORTFOLIO confidence, set by the ranking chair on the de-scoped version of each brief, which is why it can sit above the adjusted score (OPP-03 at 62 versus an adjusted 48). It answers 'how sure am I of the thing I am actually funding', not 'how sure am I of the brief as written'.

Four cautions. First, CONFIDENCE AND RANK MEASURE DIFFERENT THINGS and are deliberately allowed to disagree: OPP-03 carries the portfolio's highest confidence (62) and ranks second, while OPP-07 ranks first at 58. Anyone re-weighting toward certainty and away from newness should reverse the top two, and the portfolio says so (D-07). Second, THERE IS A CEILING: nothing exceeds 62, and no opportunity scores above 3 on risk. That is a portfolio-wide floor reflecting the unanchored evidence base, not a per-brief penalty. Third, CONFIDENCE IS NOT INDEPENDENT ACROSS ITEMS: most of these scores would move together on the same three or four internal data pulls, so they are correlated, not eight separate bets. Fourth, HIGH CONFIDENCE IS NOT A DECISION - OPP-08 carries confidence 50 and remains EXPLORE because the cheap kill test has not been run.

Finally: every claim in this portfolio is labelled either as a FINDING (evidenced, cited by signal id) or a HYPOTHESIS (inferred, uncorroborated). Where a brief's central premise is a hypothesis, it is said so explicitly - that outdoor findability rather than function is the binding constraint (OPP-02), that jersey-adjacency drives a bottoms purchase (OPP-07), that fabric GSM ever changed (OPP-03). Do not read those as facts because they sit inside a funded item.

research_gaps.gap: Unit share by inseam - by gender, by size, by market, by door type. It appears nowhere in seven specialist files, three skeptic rounds or the cross-dataset audit, in any geography.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: It is the number the length architecture of the whole portfolio turns on, and the pipeline's one formally unresolved contradiction sits directly on top of it (D-08): A07-S4 argues a short-inseam performance wave, A02-S5's own cited source says 7-9 inches, the auditor rated both the short-inseam wave and the retro/long trend UNCLEAR after striking the Accio-generated quantitative spine of the latter, and Nike's live ladder runs 6-11 inches continuously with the LONGEST length at the LOWEST price. No opportunity may be built on a length assumption until this exists.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Internal pull, no external cost: units and full-price sell-through by inseam AND by size for the basketball shorts class, full year rather than an August snapshot, Nike DTC plus Kohl's, Dick's, Academy, Hibbett, Foot Locker and Amazon, split men's/women's and performance/lifestyle door. Replicate in UK, DE, FR, AU and Greater China before any lead market is assumed. 3-4 weeks.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: NA Wholesale Demand & Supply Planning with account business teams, coordinated by Global Basketball Apparel PLM; geo replication by EMEA/APLA/GC Merchandising leads

research_gaps.gap: Realised ASP, markdown rate, full-price sell-through and weeks-of-supply by SKU, inseam, door and region. No price in this entire base was confirmed against a retrieved product page, in any geography.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: The audit found three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders coexisting and not one anchored to a page, because every retail host was egress-blocked for every agent. Five of eight briefs proposed a new price rung on that foundation, and every observable shelf datapoint contradicts them (DNA 8 inch at 50% off, DNA 6 inch realised at USD 37.50, Sabrina USD 65 clearing at USD 42.97, Kohl's Big and Tall Academy 11 inch at USD 27.75, UV Woven at AUD 44.99 against an AUD 75-80 ask). In a +2% currency-neutral business on +1% units, an unanchored price-up is an unbooked markdown, not upside. All three INVEST price positions have been struck for this reason and none can be restored without this pull.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Internal list-versus-realised ASP and markdown by SKU/inseam/region for the shorts class, eight quarters, plus wholesale sell-through from the named accounts; supplemented by one week of third-party retail price tracking on BASKETBALL shorts specifically (not athletic shorts) covering Nike, adidas, New Balance, Li-Ning, Anta and Amazon private label. 2-3 weeks internal; roughly USD 10-20k for the tracking.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: Merchandise Financial Planning and Global Pricing, with Key Account Management for the wholesale sell-through half

research_gaps.gap: Whether any make or material change actually happened, and whether the durability defect is real - returns and warranty defect codes, plus GSM/BOM/supplier-change history FY23-FY26.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: OPP-03's entire diagnosis is reverse-engineered from consumer reviews. Nobody has established that fabric weight or construction ever changed, in either direction, on any Nike shorts franchise - so the premise may simply be false. Separately, no benchmark exists for what a normal review score is (the Dick's Icon+ 6 inch 3.9 stars / 67% recommending, A04-S6, has nothing to compare against), and no one has separated genuine make failure from a high-heat-drying artifact or from fit reported as quality. This is a HYPOTHESIS carrying an INVEST.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Two parallel internal pulls: FY24-FY26 returns and warranty defect codes for Icon, DNA and DNA Academy split by seam failure, post-wash dimensional change, opacity and fit/size, benchmarked against the Nike apparel basic average and a training-shorts control; plus a GSM/BOM/supplier-change history. Add a physical teardown of 40-60 returned units. Stop the programme at the returns report if the defect codes are ordinary. 3-4 weeks, well under USD 25k.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: Nike Consumer Services returns analytics with Apparel Materials and Quality Engineering; sponsored by Basketball Apparel PLM

research_gaps.gap: Wholesale trade terms - markdown allowances, margin-protection payments and chargebacks - and therefore what share of any recovered markdown accrues to Nike rather than to the retailer.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: OPP-03's headline USD 19 per-unit recovery is booked at RETAIL markdown inside a programme weighted roughly 70/30 to WHOLESALE, so a meaningful share of it is a gift to Dick's and Foot Locker rather than Nike margin. The challenger identified this as a P&L-level error that would have shipped unchallenged in any single-owner brief. It is the explicit gate on the portfolio's highest-confidence item, and the same arithmetic silently underwrites the price-up logic in OPP-02 and OPP-08.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Pull the wholesale trade-terms and allowance file alongside the eight-quarter markdown and WOS file for the shorts class; re-model realised-revenue-per-unit at Nike realised wholesale revenue under 50%, 35% and 20% retail markdown scenarios against incremental BOM, test and QA cost. Published stop condition: kill if realised recovery per unit is not a multiple of incremental cost. 2-3 weeks, no external cost.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: NA Wholesale Finance with Merchandise Financial Planning, sponsored by Basketball Apparel PLM

research_gaps.gap: Women's fan-bottoms demand: whether the WNBA Rebel Edition Fanwear short (8 May 2026) and the Caitlin Clark short sold, what share of women's basketball fan merchandise units are BOTTOMS rather than tops, and whether the volume buyer is female at all.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: This is the settled-demand half of the top-ranked opportunity, and it is settled only on the DEMAND side. The bottoms half remains a HYPOTHESIS: the strongest term in the base ('female jersey outfit' +494%) is a TOPS term, it sits in the same Pinterest report as 'F1 aesthetic outfit' +483% and 'Brazil jersey outfit women' +302%, and the auditor instructed the basketball attribution be discarded. The Rebel Fanwear short is the closest thing to a live in-market test of this exact idea, Nike owns the number, and it appears in no file. Underneath it sits an unresolved fork the pipeline deliberately did not close (D-09): Ed Stack described 'boys and girls, young men and women' buying this product (A04-S5), which argues a unisex fan block in a women's size run rather than a women's-graded block - the opposite construction decision from the same evidence.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Near-zero-cost first-party pull, 2-3 weeks: weekly sell-through by door and by size for the Rebel Fanwear short, Clark short, WNBA Victory short, Legends Flow Mesh and Sabrina/Crossover women's, FY26 full year, plus jersey-plus-bottom basket analysis at Nike.com and via the licensing partner. Add a category-mix pull by garment type from the WNBA licensing partner and Fanatics (threshold: bottoms must exceed roughly 12% of units to justify a dedicated block). Gate any block development or tooling behind both.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: Basketball Apparel PLM with Global Merch Financial Planning and the WNBA licensing team; Fanatics category analytics for the partner half

research_gaps.gap: Europe - Nike's second geography is the primary market of under 2% of signals. No live EMEA basketball assortment, SKU count, inseam mix or price ladder; no European unit volume, ASP or sell-through for any brand; no European consumer read of any kind.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: This is the base's single largest hole and its cheapest one to start closing. Europe enters the analysis only as a compliance deadline, a markdown line (EMEA revenue -6%, Digital -24%) and a set of doors. Meanwhile EuroLeague set a fourth consecutive attendance record at 3,251,706 (+8%) with TV viewership up 82% to 122.8M, and none of it is in any file. The portfolio REJECTED OPP-05 Continental partly because its EUR 45 anchor may de-rate existing European business rather than create a rung - and nobody can currently say which. The portfolio explicitly elevated this read to a mandated action independent of any brief (D-03); the risk it names is that the genuine European finding gets rejected along with the franchise.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Sequenced and cheap-first. (1) Internal EMEA merchandising extract, 3-5 working days at effectively zero cost: basketball shorts SKU list by inseam and franchise, list price by market, realised ASP, full-price sell-through, markdown rate, Nike Direct versus wholesale - plus a same-day rack walk of three KICKZ doors, one JD Europe and one Intersport/SportScheck. (2) Direct federation registry pull (DBB, FFBB, FEB, TBF, LKF, KSS, Basketball England, Sport England Active Lives) to test whether EuroLeague's attendance record is a spectating story or a playing story. Only if both clear should syndicated panel access (EUR 120-200k) be considered.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: EMEA Merchandising and Demand Planning for the assortment pull; EMEA Category Insights for the registry work

research_gaps.gap: Greater China as a subject of evidence rather than a source of it: no Tmall, JD, Douyin or Xiaohongshu datapoint, no Chinese-language consumer voice, not one retrieved Chinese price - and an unreconciled contradiction on whether Li-Ning basketball is recovering or still falling.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: SS28's stated Worldball priority points at Greater China, and every China conclusion in this base is assembled from European and US resellers, a JD price aggregator, 2023 state media about one Guizhou village and a 2019 NBA public-relations estimate. Every China price recommendation in the portfolio should be treated as unfounded, not as an estimate. The direction of the branded segment is itself contested: A02-S3 has Li-Ning at -19% for 2025 and A04-S2 has +5% for H1 2026 - same company, adjacent periods, opposite direction. That one number decides whether Nike would be entering a recovering or a collapsing branded segment. OPP-02's lead market is formally unresolved for exactly this reason.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Reconcile the Li-Ning contradiction from the company's own full-year filings, then pull Tmall/JD/Douyin category price-band share and GMV for basketball shorts 2024-2026 for Nike, Li-Ning, Anta and 361, plus retrieved domestic RMB prices for the Wade UPF short, via a local e-commerce data provider. Roughly USD 20-35k, 3-4 weeks. Until it returns, no RMB price should be presented as a price.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: Greater China Consumer and Marketplace Insights with a local e-commerce data provider

research_gaps.gap: Claims and regulatory position: Nike's standing legal policy on printing numeric UPF and third-party certification marks, and the scope of the EU Empowering Consumers Directive (applicable 27 September 2026) over performance and durability claims as well as environmental ones.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: This is a GATE, not an input, and it is time-critical at roughly three weeks out. Nike's own claims policy defines Dri-FIT UV as 'minimum UPF 30' and declines to print a UPF number even in Australia - so OPP-02's differentiation collapses to the de-scoped merchandising fix if Legal will not reverse it, and reversing it is a platform-wide governance programme, not a hangtag change. On OPP-03, printing a durability number in the season EmpCo makes unsubstantiated durability claims specifically sanctionable would convert existing puffery ('lightweight-yet-durable', 'built for the grind') into an implied warranty across tens of millions of units - which is why the 20W badge and the guarantee were both killed. France's environmental-cost display and durability coefficient add a second clock. Separately, ACCC exposure for a non-standard wet UPF rating in Australia was examined by nobody in this base.
research_gaps.how_to_close: One combined legal read rather than three: EmpCo scope over non-environmental claims after the Green Claims Directive withdrawal; whether a published test figure constitutes a commercial guarantee of durability; the substantiation file a printed UPF 50+ plus wet/stretch addendum requires per market; an audit of existing DNA/Icon durability copy for current exposure; and the compliance review of the CURRENT hangtag and PDP language, which is required before 27 September 2026 whether or not any of these briefs proceed. 3-4 weeks internal plus EU outside counsel.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: Global Legal (Marketing Claims) with EMEA Regulatory Affairs, Product Integrity and Global Apparel Compliance

research_gaps.gap: How Nike's own event-linked basketball capsules actually performed - Paris 2024, the 2023 FIBA World Cup, Quai 54 - split BOTTOMS versus tops; plus the exact terms and renewal status of the FIBA product partnership and what LA28/USOPC licensing permits.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: OPP-06 is the only item on the board with an external clock, and both halves of its case are unverified from public data. The mechanism has a Nike-specific disconfirmation the spec never looked for: Nike guided the Paris 2024 Olympic quarter down about 10%, its first Olympic-quarter decline since at least Sydney 2000, with product in 8,000+ doors - which turns 'a dated moment pulls full price' from a proven mechanism into a rights-and-marketing-dependent one. The FIBA agreement runs 2017-2027 with no renewal found, so the leg Nike owns is closing while the leg sold as the destination belongs to Fanatics, Ralph Lauren and FOURTEEN. And whether a national-team moment attaches to SHORTS at all is inferred, never observed - the strongest fan-fashion signal in the base is a TOPS term.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Two zero-cost internal reads that must happen this quarter: (1) internal sell-through pull from Merchandising/Demand and Supply for the three named capsules, cut by BOTTOMS as a share of capsule units and their full-price rate at week 8 versus the capsule's tops - if bottoms cleared at markdown in all three, kill it; (2) pull the FIBA partnership contract and term sheet from Sports Marketing/Legal, asking specifically whether the 3x3 carve-out to FOURTEEN limits anything, and whether renewal past 2027 is in negotiation. Add structured buyer interviews on whether a wholesale merchant will place a non-replenishable FA27 capsule at all.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: Nike Merchandising Analytics with Jordan Brand (for Quai 54); Sports Marketing (FIBA account) and Legal/Licensing for the rights half

research_gaps.gap: The SS28 seasonal calendar itself - line-lock, sample review, futures close, factory commit and delivery dates - which appears in none of the seven specialist files and was supplied only by the cross-dataset audit.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: It is load-bearing under two decisions and unverified under both. OPP-04's ENTIRE case is that an Australia-first drop returns a season of sell-through before the SS28 global buy commits; on the calendar as understood, the buy closes around the month the Australian range would land, with line-lock a year before that, which makes the proving-ground mechanism arithmetically void and drops it to WATCH. OPP-06's gate has the same shape: a week-8 read on a Jul-Sep 2027 Doha drop arrives Oct-Nov 2027, roughly when the SS28 wholesale books have to be written. Every date in this portfolio must be confirmed before anything is planned against it - including the two rankings that turn on them.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Pull the SS28 and SS29 seasonal calendars from Global Apparel Product Creation and the geo merchandising teams; produce a one-page timeline showing which decisions are still open on each date, overlaid with the proposed Australian delivery window and the Doha event window (27 August - 12 September 2027). Zero incremental cost, 1-2 weeks. If OPP-06's gate is under four weeks wide, that programme must be re-underwritten as a single Doha activation.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: Global Apparel PLM with Demand and Supply Management and APLA Merchandising

research_gaps.gap: Direct verification of live catalogues that were egress-blocked - Nike Team Sports and BSN above all, but the failure is systemic: not one price, spec or review claim in the base was confirmed against a retrieved page.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: The single most consequential systemic error in this pipeline ran in the NEGATIVE direction: six 'this does not exist' claims were all false and all would have been caught by one query against Nike's own catalogue. FN2659 alone closed four independently declared white spaces. That cuts both ways at the gate - OPP-01's unanimous REJECT rests on search-snippet reads of six blocked domains, and the portfolio says openly that a ten-minute direct look at the Nike Team Sports and BSN catalogues could move that item more than anything else in the ranking. A kill built on the same instrument that produced the false whitespace deserves the same scepticism.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Open the catalogues directly from an unrestricted connection and export rather than summarise: Nike Team Sports basketball Bottoms category tree with every SKU, colourway, dealer net, size grade and FY24-FY26 units, plus the identical pull on adidas Team and Under Armour Team. Run the parallel live SKU-and-fixture audit for OPP-07 (12 doors plus screen-captures of the Fanatics/WNBAStore/Nike WNBA pages). 1-2 days for the catalogue pull at effectively zero cost; roughly USD 5-8k and 1-2 weeks for the fixture audit.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: Nike Team Sports category merchandising with a BSN account manager; US Merchandising / Marketplace Ops field team for the fan-wall audit

research_gaps.gap: Whether anyone buys an outdoor-specified basketball short at a premium, and what stretch and saturation actually do to UPF at basketball-specific strain.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: There is no sell-through, conversion, search-volume or stated-preference evidence for outdoor-specified basketball shorts anywhere in this base - for Nike, Li-Ning, Anta or anyone. OPP-02's demand case is inferred entirely from participation, physiology and a competitor's assortment decision, and its central premise - that findability rather than function is the binding constraint - is an explicit HYPOTHESIS nobody has measured. The technical differentiator has already been narrowed: AATCC 183 provides a wet test state and ASTM D6603 conditions and documents the stretch effect, so 'UPF certified wet and stretched' is a purchasable test election a competitor can answer in one cycle, and ARPANSA certifies per material AND per colour, which is economically incompatible with a seasonal local-graphic strategy. Every sweat measurement in hand comes from air-conditioned North American gyms with overwhelmingly male samples and is being used to specify product for Guangzhou, Manila and Delhi.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Cheapest first: a rack-legibility test with the lead retail partners (does a buyer or consumer identify outdoor function in under five seconds with no product copy) before any lab spend, since legibility is the actual funded thesis. Then, only if the certification route is revived, three constructions x three colourways to an accredited lab under AS 4399:2020, AATCC 183 wet and a biaxial-stretch addendum, recording explicitly which colourways fail 50+. Court-intercept observation in a CunBA-belt city, Manila and Phoenix (n>=150 per market) to test whether a UPF claim registers as a reason to buy a SHORT at all, and to quantify on-body phone carry, which A06-S4 left explicitly unmeasured.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: Consumer Insights (Global Basketball) with Key Account Management for the legibility half; Nike ATG materials engineering with an accredited lab if the certification route is revived

research_gaps.gap: Sizing of the coverage-first, extended-size and modest-dress population, and whether that buyer is choosing coverage or choosing price - plus layering prevalence below elite level.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: OPP-08's need case is a HYPOTHESIS resting on three qualitative items, two of them from 2014-2017, and the AND1 read rests on one anonymous review saying 'affordable and cultural'. If the driver is price, a USD 55 Nike short addresses the wrong motive entirely - and Kohl's realises USD 27.75 on the Big and Tall Academy 11 inch against a USD 55 ask, a near-doubling with no willingness-to-pay evidence anywhere in the base or on the open web. Nike has also run a modest extended-size collection since 2017 without ever adding a long women's basketball bottom, which is nine years of revealed preference nobody has explained. Separately, layering prevalence at high-school, club and college level is entirely unmeasured, and it is the binding unknown under both OPP-01's architecture and OPP-03's liner-deletion funding mechanism.
research_gaps.how_to_close: Run the cheap kill test before the research: list one 11-inch inside the premium DNA franchise at USD 50-55 for a single season in existing fabric, held on nike.com rather than bought into physical doors, measured against a held-out control for cannibalisation of the Academy 11 inch. In parallel, decompose the price file (franchise effect versus length effect at constant length and constant franchise, US and UK) at zero cost. Only if it moves should conjoint (n~800, two cells: AND1/Walmart 2XL-5XL buyers and Nike DNA Academy buyers) and coded broadcast observation of tights prevalence be funded.
research_gaps.owner_suggestion: Basketball Apparel PLM with Digital Merchandising and one key account for the listing test; Merchandising Financial Planning for the price-file decomposition; Global Consumer Insights only afterwards

methodology_limitations: PUBLIC WEB EVIDENCE ONLY, AND MOSTLY UNRETRIEVED. Every specialist and skeptic worked from the open web with no access to Nike systems. Worse, the retail hosts that would have anchored the analysis - Dick's, Foot Locker, Nike.com product pages, store.nba.com, Fanatics, kickz.com, niketeam.nike.com, BSN, assets.fiba.basketball - were egress-blocked for every agent, so not one price, spec or review claim in the base was confirmed against a page that was actually opened. The price architecture is built from search-result summaries, and at least one figure (the USD 75 Aero-FIT basketball short) appears to be the search engine echoing the query language back. Read every price and every catalogue claim in this report as provisional.

NO NIKE INTERNAL DATA OF ANY KIND. There is no first-party commercial data anywhere in the base: no sell-through, no unit mix by inseam, no markdown rate by SKU, no returns or return reasons, no realised ASP, no size-curve fill, no repeat-purchase interval, no channel split for the shorts class, no BOM or GSM history, no wholesale trade terms. The one category this entire programme is about is the one category with no quantitative evidence in it. Consequently the correct reading of the whole exercise is that it generated a prioritised research agenda and a set of de-scoped hypotheses, not a validated portfolio.

US-HEAVY SOURCES, UNCORRECTED. Roughly three quarters of the evidence is US-derived once 'Global' signals are attributed honestly. Europe is the primary market of under 2% of signals and appears only as a compliance deadline, a markdown line and a set of doors. Latin America is entirely absent. The Gulf appears once, as a property blog, while the SS28 window's largest owned basketball moment lands in Doha. Greater China is the second-most-cited geography and the least-directly-evidenced - no Tmall, JD, Douyin or Xiaohongshu data, no Chinese-language source, no retrieved Chinese price - yet carries the stated Worldball priority and specific RMB recommendations. Any 'global' claim in this report is currently unfalsifiable outside the United States.

SOURCE QUALITY IS UNEVEN AND SOME OF IT SHOULD BE TREATED AS ZERO. The audit found report mills and AI content farms load-bearing in six of seven domains (Technavio in four vintages, Verified Market Research, Dataintelo, SkyQuest, market.us, plus Accio - Alibaba's AI B2B sourcing engine - reused across five signals in two domains). Category sizing estimates from these sources disagree by roughly 2x for the same year. Marketplace listings were repeatedly treated as market data: Amazon best-seller impressions with no rank or unit figures, auto-generated retailer inseam facets read as merchandising strategy, a navigation menu read as a styling signal. Roughly a fifth of the base is quantitative in appearance only and carries false precision into decks.

DUPLICATE-AS-CORROBORATION. The base's most dangerous structural flaw is that where three domains agree, they are usually reading the same document. The women's case, the market-size case, the China participation case, the retro-length case and the local-labels case were each one source agreed with three times - and each read to a decision-maker as triangulation until the cross-dataset audit separated them. Signal counts in this report are therefore not independent votes.

AI AGENTS, WITH A DOCUMENTED SYSTEMIC BIAS. Twenty-plus autonomous agents produced this analysis. Their shared failure mode was proposing product Nike already ships: six 'this does not exist' claims were all false, all in the negative direction, and all would have been caught by one query against Nike's own catalogue. Absence of evidence was repeatedly written up as evidence of absence under a documented condition where no product page could be opened. The red team corrected much of this - which is exactly why every adjusted confidence score fell - but a kill built on the same blocked-domain instrument (notably OPP-01) inherits the same weakness.

SINGLE RUN, NO REPLICATION, AND THE PIPELINE'S OWN CALIBRATION IS A JUDGEMENT. This is one pass: seven specialists, seven skeptics, one audit, three lenses, one synthesis, one development and one challenge round per opportunity, three rankers and one chair. Nothing was re-run to test stability. Three rankers scoring the same eight opportunities returned three different top-threes, which is itself evidence that the ordering is weight-sensitive rather than robust - the chair's weights are stated so the arithmetic is auditable, but a different chair with defensible weights would reorder the top two. Where the rankers split, the portfolio decided rather than averaged, and those decisions (D-01 through D-10) are judgements, not findings.

TIME-BASE DRIFT AND A MISSING CALENDAR. Stale sources were used as current across the base - 2024 WNBA figures in 2026, a 2019 collection as current competitive design language, a 2014 athlete interview, 2015-2017 prototypes as a live gap, 2023 tournament coverage as 'still spreading'. Separately, the SS28 calendar and the two largest basketball moments of the cycle (FIBA World Cup Qatar, 27 August - 12 September 2027; LA28 opening 14 July 2028) appear in none of the seven specialist files and were supplied only by the audit - so the sequencing arguments that depend on them are built on dates this pipeline did not verify.

THE COST SIDE IS ABSENT. The word 'tariff' appears nowhere in the marketplace specialist's output, in a year when the US de minimis exemption ended, apparel from China carries roughly a 53.5% duty stack, and Nike is absorbing an estimated USD 1.5B annualised tariff cost with a 120bp gross-margin headwind. No landed-cost input exists for any market, and no EU cost-side input exists at all. Every price position in all eight briefs was set without one.
recommended_validation_sequence: WEEK 0 - START THE TWO CLOCKS THAT ARE ALREADY RUNNING, BEFORE ANY RESEARCH. (a) Commission the EmpCo and claims legal review today: it applies 27 September 2026, roughly three weeks out, and it is a compliance requirement for Nike's CURRENT basketball shorts hangtag and PDP copy whether or not any brief here proceeds. It gates OPP-02 and OPP-03. (b) Pull the FIBA partnership contract and term sheet and confirm renewal status past 2027, and kill the LA28 / VALLEY leg of OPP-06 today on rights (Fanatics, Ralph Lauren, FOURTEEN) so nobody builds a deck around it. Both are internal, zero external cost, 1-3 weeks.

WEEKS 1-4 - THE FIVE INTERNAL PULLS THAT UNBLOCK HALF THE BOARD. Run these in parallel; they are data Nike already owns and cost time, not money. (1) Unit share by inseam, gender, size and market. (2) Realised ASP, markdown rate and full-price sell-through by SKU and door, full year not an August snapshot. (3) Returns and warranty by defect code plus BOM/GSM history FY23-FY26. (4) Rebel Fanwear and Caitlin Clark shorts sell-through, plus bottoms share of women's basketball fan units. (5) Whether the Paris 2024 and 2023 FIBA World Cup basketball BOTTOMS cleared at markdown. Add the SS28/SS29 calendar extract and the live Nike Team Sports / BSN catalogue pull. Five of eight briefs were talked down by the red team for reasons these would settle in either direction.

WEEKS 1-4, PARALLEL AND SEPARATELY OWNED - THE TWO FREE GEOGRAPHIC READS. (a) Nike's own live EMEA basketball assortment, SKU count, inseam mix and realised price ladder, plus a one-day rack walk of three KICKZ doors, one JD Europe and one Intersport - 3-5 working days, effectively zero cost, and it closes the portfolio's largest structural hole. (b) Eight quarters of Nike AU and wholesale sell-through by inseam, gender, price and door from Rebel, JD AU and Foot Locker AU - this replaces the entire OPP-04 programme with a phone call and instruments Australia as a lead door inside OPP-02. Neither needs an opportunity attached to it.

WEEK 4 GATE - RE-MODEL BEFORE ANY COMMITMENT. Rebuild OPP-03's business case at Nike REALISED WHOLESALE revenue using the actual allowance recovery rate, not at retail markdown. Published stop condition, agreed in advance: if realised recovery per unit is not a multiple of incremental cost, or if the returns defect codes come back ordinary and no GSM drift is found, stop the programme. This is the single decision most likely to prevent a P&L error, and it must clear before any make-standard spend.

WEEKS 4-8 - ACT ON WHAT NEEDS NO GATE, TEST WHAT DOES. Book OPP-02's de-scoped action into the SS28 assortment immediately: name the franchise, ladder FN2659 from one inseam to 5/7/9, extend the women's block, build the rack legibility system, hold price. It needs no research gate and carries essentially no incremental inventory liability. Do NOT fund the certification programme or the price-up. In parallel run OPP-08's two-week price-file decomposition (franchise effect versus length effect, US and UK) and then its cheapest kill test - one 11-inch listed inside the premium DNA franchise at USD 50-55, existing fabric, nike.com only, against a held-out control.

WEEKS 4-10 - DECIDE DOHA, AND ONLY DOHA. On the event-capsule sell-through read and the wholesale buyer conversations, decide the OPP-06 Doha leg this quarter. If the bottoms cleared at markdown across Paris 2024, the 2023 World Cup and Quai 54, move it to REJECT. If a wholesale merchant will not place a non-replenishable FA27 capsule, move it to REJECT. This is the only item with an external clock and it decides itself if nobody decides it.

WEEKS 8-16 - ONLY AFTER THE FREE DATA RETURNS, FUND CONSUMER RESEARCH. Gate all paid consumer work behind the pulls above. In order of value: the rack-legibility and monadic price-intent test for OPP-02 (the question that decides whether any price step exists); the OPP-07 wear-and-styling test on rise, leg-line and hem with a jersey TUCKED, including a parallel male fan-buyer cell to settle the women's-graded versus unisex fork (D-09); court-intercept observation in a CunBA-belt city, Manila and Phoenix to test whether a UPF claim registers on a SHORT and to quantify on-body phone carry. Do not fund block development or tooling before the OPP-07 pulls clear.

BEFORE ANY OF IT IS BOOKED - RUN THE ADJACENCY REVIEW. Put the surviving specs on one wall and map SKU, silhouette, inseam, consumer, door and price. Four of eight briefs propose product against the same DNA/Icon rail: OPP-08's 11 inch would hang beside a USD 27.75 Academy 11 inch in the same door and palette; OPP-07's block risks splitting demand against Clark, Sabrina and Rebel Edition programmes already funded; OPP-06 stripped of its date is OPP-01 plus OPP-02 plus OPP-07/08 competing for one buy. Any two funded without an explicit adjacency plan buy the same demand twice - which is how a line loses productivity while adding SKUs. Half a day, zero cost, and it belongs before the money moves.

STANDING RULE FOR THE WHOLE SEQUENCE - NO LENGTH AND NO PRICE UNTIL THE DATA EXISTS. Unit share by inseam appears nowhere in seven specialist files, three skeptic rounds or the audit, in any market, and the inseam-direction contradiction (D-08) is formally unresolved. No opportunity may be built on a length assumption, and no price rung may be presented as a recommendation, until pulls 1 and 2 return. Every price in all three INVESTs has already been struck on this basis; restoring one requires the pull, not an argument.
